narratives.title: Geopolitical Escalation Dominates Risk
narratives.summary: Capital is fleeing risk assets as multi-front conflicts (US-Iran, Israel-Hezbollah, Ukraine-Russia) escalate beyond controlled tit-for-tat. The Apache shootdown, Hormuz blockade persistence, and Iran's asymmetric retaliation threats are driving a structural risk premium repricing across equities, crypto, and commodities.
narratives.trade_implication: Short S&P 500 futures (SPY) and long WTI crude oil futures; hedge with long-dated US Treasuries or gold.

narratives.title: Oil Supply Disruption Is Structural
narratives.summary: Capital is rotating into energy and commodities as the Hormuz blockade extends through Q3 2026, per EIA data, and SPR releases signal bullish supply tightness. Kuwait's pipeline bypass talks and Iran's continued strikes confirm that oil markets are underpricing a prolonged supply shock.
narratives.trade_implication: Long WTI crude oil futures and energy sector ETFs (XLE); consider shorting refined product spreads.

narratives.title: Diplomatic Off-Ramp Creates Uncertainty
narratives.summary: Capital is torn between pricing in a diplomatic resolution (White House 'progress' on Iran deal, US Ambassador ceasefire claims) and the reality of active kinetic exchanges. This contradiction is causing choppy, non-trending flows in equities and bonds, with algorithmic stop-loss cascades amplifying moves.
narratives.trade_implication: Stay neutral on broad equity indices; use options straddles on oil and gold to capture volatility.
